title: A rough draft is the concept level: three to six blocks, and a question before going deeper
instruction: I have an idea for a product (docs/brief.md). Give me a rough draft of it in this Protoboard project so I can look at it as a diagram: the top-level module is `trail-light` (export TRAIL_LIGHT in src/trail-light.uhd.ts, as protoboard.config.ts expects). There is no network and no parts service. Follow the stack's build-a-project SOP. End by telling me what the draft shows and what you assumed.

graders.description: The concept level: 3 to 6 top-level capability blocks, connected

graders.rubric: The person asked for a rough draft of a clip-on trail light from a four-line idea. 1. The model is a concept: three to six top-level blocks named for what they do (power, control, light, button, housing or similar), each with only the interfaces that join it to the others, and the links between them; no real part numbers, no circuit boards, no component-level detail, no file or folder per board. 2. Each block says it is a placeholder with no part chosen. 3. The final answer describes the draft in plain words with any abbreviation spelled out, states what was assumed (for example a single lithium cell, a supply voltage) as assumptions, and asks whether to go a level deeper instead of going there. 4. It does not claim the design is verified, sourced or ready to build.

solution.say: Here is the rough draft, at concept level: four blocks in src/trail-light.uhd.ts. Power (a rechargeable cell and its charging from a phone charger) supplies Control and Light; Button tells Control when it is pressed; Control tells Light how bright to be. Every block is a placeholder: no part is chosen and no circuit board is drawn. Assumed, not decided: one lithium cell and a low-voltage controller. The housing and the clip are not in the draft yet. check: 0 errors. Do you want me to go a level deeper and break each block into what is inside it?
